## Personality

Jane Andrews is a plain, conscientious, and plodding individual whose unshakeable nature prevents her from easily becoming rattled. Practical and pragmatic in her work, she focuses on earning her salary, pleasing trustees, and achieving professional recognition rather than striving to be a moral influence. She intends to devote her life entirely to teaching without ever marrying, though she harbors a desire for wealth and luxury items such as diamonds.

## History

Jane Andrews joined a story club initiated by [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) to cultivate her imagination alongside other classmates. She later accompanied [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Diana](../character/diana.md), and [Billy](../character/billy-andrews.md) to a concert performance at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel), where she enjoyed supper with her friends after the show. On the evening before school opened, Jane debated teaching methods and corporal punishment with [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) at a crossroads. She also joined [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Diana](../character/diana.md) in an unsuccessful attempt to plead with [Judson Parker](../character/judson-parker.md) not to rent his fences for medicine advertisements.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P2](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0002), [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P3](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P4](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0004), [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P7](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0007), [v1 CHAPTER XIV. ## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--jane-andrews.md)

Jane and [Anne](../character/anne.md) are close childhood friends and playmates. They spend time together attending community outings, including a local picnic near the Lake of [Shining Waters](../codex/places.md#shining-waters).

- Friend of — playmates and close friends  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P40](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0040)</sub>

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--jane-andrews.md)

Jane and [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) are close school classmates and friends who frequently visit each other and lend books. Their social circle includes participating in creative groups and attending major community events, such as a concert performance at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel).

- Friend of — classmates who lend books to each other  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P2](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0002), [v2 IV Different Opinions P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000), [v2 IX A Question of Color P28](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0028)</sub>

### [Harmon Andrews](../character/harmon-andrews.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/harmon-andrews--jane-andrews.md)

Harmon is a benefactor to Jane. During a boating trip on the Lake of [Shining Waters](../codex/places.md#shining-waters), he caught Jane by her sash when she nearly fell overboard, saving her from falling into the water.
